title: Losing My Shape
tagline: The fragile moment when dreams, memories and human connections slowly begin to fade.
storyTitle: Born in a small studio room

story.t: "Losing My Shape" reflects the fragile moment when dreams, memories and human connections slowly begin to fade, when everything familiar starts to lose its outline.

Born in a small studio room in Purkersdorf, near Vienna, the song began as an intimate recording with only a few musicians, a quiet space and a powerful emotional atmosphere. What started as a fragile demo has now found its moment to step into the world.

The song takes us on a haunting journey through uncertainty, isolation and the search for direction. Yet within this feeling of being lost lies a deeper human struggle: the desire to hold on, to keep rising from the cold, and to find meaning when everything seems to fade away.

credits: Andreas Wukics-Hagen, Wolfgang Laab, Karen Fellinger

title: Nothing Is Forever
tagline: An anthem about impermanence, driven by rock elements and a pulsating 132 BPM rhythm.

story.t: "Nothing Is Forever" is an anthem about impermanence. Driven by energetic rock elements and a pulsating 132 BPM rhythm, the track captures both intensity and emotion.

It explores the constant ups and downs of life: love and laughter, pain and silence, sunshine and rain. Nothing stays the same, everything is in motion, and that is exactly where the beauty of the moment lies. The song reminds us to embrace the present before it slips away.
It is dedicated to Andreas’ late father, whom he deeply admired as a role model and with whom he shared many years performing together on stage. In loving memory.

title: Rainbow Eyes EDM Club Mix
tagline: Rainbow Eyes, rebuilt for the dance floor.

story.t: The EDM Club Mix takes "Rainbow Eyes" from the late-night drive to the dance floor: the same melody and longing, carried by a driving club beat and bright synths.
Read the story behind the original song on the "Rainbow Eyes" page.

title: Rainbow Eyes
tagline: A song about the magic of being lost in beautiful eyes.

story.t: With "Rainbow Eyes", WUHA delivers an emotional pop anthem full of longing, wonder and warmth. The song captures the intensity of a single look, the kind that leaves you breathless and lost in a beautiful mystery.

Driven by a catchy melody and heartfelt lyrics, the track floats between dreamy verses and a powerful chorus. With screaming bends and searing tone, Wolfgang unleashes a guitar solo that turns the track into a full-on rock anthem. Soft harmonies and the beautiful background voice of Petra Suk, known as Suki from Two In One, round it off.
Musically, "Rainbow Eyes" blends pop and soft rock with a touch of 80s nostalgia: modern in production, timeless in feeling.

title: Caroline Extended Club Mix
tagline: Caroline, stretched out for the dance floor.
storyTitle: A 1989 love song on the dance floor

story.t: The Extended Club Mix gives "Caroline" more room to breathe: a longer intro, a steady four-to-the-floor beat and the voice of Marc Voc floating over glowing synths.
Read how the song began in a Vienna club in 1989 on the "Caroline" page.

title: Caroline (feat. Marc Voc)
tagline: A love song from 1989, reborn more than three decades later.

story.t: This song was written in 1989 when I was in love with a girl I regularly met at my favourite club, Poeblo, on Karlsplatz in Vienna. Together with her friend Petra, she was always my personal highlight in the club. We were good friends and often talked for hours, but it was never enough for a kiss. I was still far too shy back then. I soon lost sight of Caroline, but the song stayed with me.

In December 2024, a coronavirus infection forced me to quarantine for a week. I used this time to produce the song again with modern means, with Ableton Live and Pro Tools. For the analog sound I won over my former band colleague Wolfgang, for me always the Austrian Steve Lukather from Toto. The music video was lovingly produced by LIFESTYLE TV.
The secret of the lead vocal

It took a long time to find the right voice. In the end we booked a professional singer online. He loved our demo and sent us three takes: an international dream voice. He works on international projects and needs to remain anonymous, so we gave him the name Marc Voc.

Caroline herself never heard the song, but her best friend at the time did: Petra Suk (Suki) of Two In One. A love song that began more than three decades ago now brings the magic of the past into the present.
